desc:
Given an array nums of non-negative integers and an integer target, count the non-empty contiguous subarrays whose bitwise XOR of all elements equals target.

nums = [4, 2, 2, 6, 4], target = 6
matching subarrays: [4, 2], [2, 2, 6], [6], [4, 2, 2, 6, 4]
result = 4
constraints: The answer is at most n(n + 1) / 2 and fits in a 32-bit integer
hints: XOR behaves like addition without carries: it is associative and every value is its own inverse (x ^ x = 0).
Define px[i] as the XOR of the first i elements. The XOR of a block i..j-1 is px[j] ^ px[i].
The block XORs to target exactly when px[i] = px[j] ^ target. Keep a hash map counting earlier prefix XORs (start with {0: 1}) and, for each new prefix, add the count of prefix ^ target.
editorial: Because a ^ a = 0, the XOR of a block equals the XOR of two prefix values: px[j] ^ px[i]. The subarray ending at position j therefore has XOR target for each earlier prefix with value px[j] ^ target.

This is the same idea as counting subarrays with a given sum, with subtraction replaced by XOR. Maintain a counter of prefix XOR values seen so far (the empty prefix, value 0, counts once). For each element update the running XOR, add count[xor ^ target] to the answer, and then record the running XOR. The pass is O(n) time and O(n) space. Note that target = 0 needs no special case: you simply count equal prefix XORs.
